adventure.title: Float the Guadalupe River at Gruene
adventure.description: Grab a tube and a cooler from Rockin' R River Rides and let three lazy miles of spring-fed green water carry you past cypress trees and the oldest dance hall in Texas.
adventure.bonus: Everyone ties their tubes together for the whole float — no breaking the chain.

adventure.title: Tube the Comal River in New Braunfels
adventure.description: The shortest river in Texas is also the most fun — a fast, clear two-hour loop through Landa Park with a tube chute at the end.
adventure.bonus: Everyone goes down the tube chute backwards.

adventure.title: Wild Cave Tour at Natural Bridge Caverns
adventure.description: Skip the paved walkway and crawl the undeveloped passages with a headlamp and knee pads — muddy, tight and unforgettable.
adventure.bonus: Everyone kills their headlamp for sixty seconds of absolute dark.

adventure.title: Paddle the Medina River Natural Area
adventure.description: A quiet, shaded stretch of bald cypress and limestone bluff fifteen minutes from downtown, where you're far more likely to see a heron than another paddler.
adventure.bonus: Go ten minutes without speaking and count how many birds you hear.

adventure.title: Summit Enchanted Rock at Sunrise
adventure.description: Climb a 425-foot pink granite dome in the dark and watch the Hill Country turn gold beneath you from the top of the second-largest batholith in the country.
adventure.bonus: Stay silent for the last hundred feet of the climb.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike the Eisenhower Park Trails
adventure.description: Rocky, rooty singletrack climbing through the Hill Country edge of the city, with an observation tower at the top as your reward.
adventure.bonus: Ride the whole loop without unclipping.

adventure.title: Indoor Skydive at iFLY San Antonio
adventure.description: Two minutes in a vertical wind tunnel is the closest thing to freefall you can get without a plane, and it's genuinely harder than it looks.
adventure.bonus: Loser of the group's best-flyer vote buys the round after.

culture.title: Friday Night at the San Antonio Museum of Art
culture.description: A converted Lone Star brewery on the river holding one of the best Latin American and Asian art collections in the country, open late on Fridays.
culture.bonus: Pick the one piece you'd steal and defend the choice.

culture.title: The Alamo at Dusk
culture.description: Go at closing time when the tour crowds thin, and the limestone chapel finally reads as the small, strange, 300-year-old mission it actually is.
culture.bonus: Find one detail on the facade that nobody photographs.

culture.title: Fiesta San Antonio
culture.description: Eleven days of parades, oyster bakes, cascarones and Night in Old San Antonio — the whole city stops working and puts on a flower crown.
culture.bonus: Collect at least five Fiesta medals from strangers.

culture.title: Spurs Game at the Frost Bank Center
culture.description: Five championship banners, the loudest building in Texas basketball, and a city that treats this team as civic identity rather than entertainment.
culture.bonus: Learn one Spurs chant before tip-off and use it.

culture.title: Día de los Muertos at Hemisfair
culture.description: San Antonio throws one of the largest Day of the Dead celebrations in the US — altars, processions and marigolds across the downtown park.
culture.bonus: Read every name on one ofrenda before you move on.

culture.title: Western Art at the Briscoe
culture.description: Santa Anna's sword, Pancho Villa's saddle and a riverside sculpture courtyard — the mythology of the West, assembled carefully and without kitsch.
culture.bonus: Find the object with the best story and tell it to the group.

culture.title: A Show at the Majestic Theatre
culture.description: A 1929 atmospheric movie palace with a ceiling painted as a Mediterranean night sky, complete with drifting clouds and stars.
culture.bonus: Get there early enough to watch the ceiling stars come on.

culture.title: The Rose Window at Mission San José
culture.description: The 'Queen of the Missions' is the grandest of the five UNESCO-listed Spanish colonial missions, and its carved rose window is the finest stonework in Texas.
culture.bonus: Walk the full perimeter wall before you go inside.

chill.title: Slow Morning at the San Antonio Botanical Garden
chill.description: Thirty-eight acres of Texas native landscapes, a conservatory of glass pyramids and a family garden that's quietly one of the best in the South.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest tree on the grounds and sit under it for ten minutes.

chill.title: Golden Hour at Confluence Park
chill.description: Petal-shaped concrete vaults arc over the spot where San Pedro Creek meets the river — an architectural showpiece that almost nobody visits.
chill.bonus: Lie on your back under the pavilion and look straight up.

chill.title: Sunset from the Tower of the Americas
chill.description: 750 feet up, the whole Hill Country horizon goes orange and the River Walk turns into a thread of light below you.
chill.bonus: Pick out three landmarks before you look at the map.

chill.title: Read in the Enchilada Red Library
chill.description: Ricardo Legorreta's Central Library is a stack of bright red geometry with skylit atriums and window seats made for an afternoon with a book.
chill.bonus: Pull a book off a shelf at random and read the first page.

chill.title: River Barge at Dusk
chill.description: Let a GO RIO barge carry you under the cypress and stone bridges of the River Walk just as the lights come on — touristy, and completely worth it.
chill.bonus: Wave at every single person on the walkway.

chill.title: Picnic Under the Oaks at Brackenridge Park
chill.description: 343 acres of old oaks, river bends and stone footbridges — San Antonio's backyard since 1899, and still the easiest place in the city to do nothing.
chill.bonus: Bring one thing for the picnic that nobody else would think to bring.

social.title: Two-Step at Cowboys Dancehall
social.description: A vast honky-tonk with a mechanical bull, a live stage and a dance floor where everyone genuinely knows the steps — take the free lesson first.

social.title: Underground Jazz at Jazz, TX
social.description: A basement supper club under the Pearl's old brewery cellars, with live jazz, western swing and a room that feels like a secret.
social.bonus: Request a song from the band.

social.title: Rooftop Cocktails at The Moon's Daughter
social.description: The Thompson's rooftop bar looks straight down the river at the Tobin Center, and the drinks are far better than the view alone would require.
social.bonus: Order whatever the bartender is proudest of.

social.title: Speakeasy Night at The Modernist
social.description: A precise, low-lit cocktail room where the menu reads like a design brief and the bartenders can talk you through every dilution choice.
social.bonus: Ask for a drink built around your least favourite spirit.

social.title: Late Night at Hi-Tones
social.description: A converted house with a patio, cheap drinks and a stage that books everything from cumbia to punk — San Antonio's most reliably fun dive.
social.bonus: Stay for a band you've never heard of.

social.title: Craft Cocktails at Bar 1919
social.description: Tucked under the Blue Star Arts Complex, this is the bar that taught San Antonio to take cocktails seriously — dark, low-ceilinged and very good.
social.bonus: Describe your ideal drink in three words and let them build it.

social.title: Dance Night at the Bonham Exchange
social.description: Three floors of an 1880s German social hall turned legendary nightclub, a block from the Alamo and running since 1981.
social.bonus: Dance on all three floors before you leave.

social.title: Pints at Weathered Souls Brewing
social.description: The San Antonio taproom behind the Black Is Beautiful stout collaboration that went global — good beer, long tables, easy conversation.
social.bonus: Start a conversation with someone at the next table.

foodie.title: Enchiladas and Margaritas at Rosario's
foodie.description: A loud, pink, thirty-year San Antonio institution where the enchiladas verdes and the house margarita have outlasted every trend in the city.

foodie.title: Pizza and Natural Wine at Il Forno
foodie.description: A tiny Southtown room turning out blistered Neapolitan pies from a wood oven, with a short, sharp natural wine list to match.
foodie.bonus: Let the server pick the wine, sight unseen.

foodie.title: Brisket at 2M Smokehouse
foodie.description: South Side barbecue that put San Antonio on the Texas map — post oak brisket alongside sausage stuffed with Oaxaca cheese and serrano.
foodie.bonus: Order one thing off the menu nobody at the table recognises.

foodie.title: Charcuterie Night at Cured
foodie.description: House-cured meats hanging in the window of the Pearl's old administration building, served as a board big enough to argue over.
foodie.bonus: Try the one cured meat you can't pronounce.

foodie.title: Barbecue Road Trip to Burnt Bean Co.
foodie.description: Thirty-five minutes east to Seguin for brisket and Tex-Mex-inflected smoked plates that rank among the best in the state.
foodie.bonus: Whoever drives picks the entire order.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Mixtli
foodie.description: A rotating multi-course journey through a single region and era of Mexican cuisine, researched like a dissertation and plated like art.
foodie.bonus: No phones out for the entire meal.

foodie.title: Morning Pastry at Bakery Lorraine
foodie.description: Macarons, kouign-amann and very good coffee in the old brewery courtyard at the Pearl — the best twenty minutes of a San Antonio morning.
foodie.bonus: Buy a macaron in a flavour you'd normally skip.

foodie.title: Tacos at Carnitas Lonja
foodie.description: Michoacán-style carnitas cooked in a copper cazo and served on handmade tortillas at a converted house on the South Side — order by the pound.
foodie.bonus: Eat one taco with nothing on it but salt and lime.

8ball.title: Wildcard: The Puffy Taco Pilgrimage
8ball.description: San Antonio invented the puffy taco and two restaurants still argue over it — eat at Ray's Drive Inn and Henry's Puffy Tacos in one afternoon and settle it yourselves.
8ball.bonus: Everyone declares a winner before the second stop, then has to defend it after.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Barge Roulette
8ball.description: Board a River Walk barge, get off at a stop nobody chose on purpose, and the first place you see with a door open is where you're eating.
8ball.bonus: No looking up reviews before you walk in.
